premises.claim: The operator believes having Jo hold the sensor will close the gate and asks Jo to do so for that end.

In ordinary practical-reasoning analysis, an agent intentionally employs another as a means when the agent requests the other’s action in pursuit of an end the agent believes that action will help bring about, regardless of whether the means will actually work.
The operator’s request that Jo hold the sensor therefore counts as intentionally employing Jo as a means toward gate closure, even though the sensor is broken and the means will fail.

response.bridge: From the operator’s belief-motivated request (premise 1) together with the interpretive account of ‘employing as a means’ (premise 2), it follows (premise 3) that Jo is indeed intentionally employed as a means.
qualifications: This conclusion presumes the standard intention-as-means criterion that relies on the agent’s practical reasoning rather than the objective efficacy of the means.
response.strongest_conclusion: Jo is intentionally employed as a means within the stipulated practical reasoning, despite the sensor’s malfunction.
remaining_questions: Would a stricter theory of means-employment require that the agent have a reasonable, rather than merely actual, belief in the means’ efficacy?
